method.promptSuffix: Answer in at most three sentences, and name the commit or rule you relied on if you can.
method.inputTokens: the sum of inputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens over every model in modelUsage of the --output-format json result (usage.input_tokens + usage.cache_creation_input_tokens + usage.cache_read_input_tokens when there is no modelUsage); the page shows this. A run whose top-level usage differs also keeps usageInputTokens.
method.outputTokens: the sum of outputTokens over every model in modelUsage (usage.output_tokens when there is none); the page shows this. A run whose top-level usage differs also keeps usageOutputTokens.
method.usageByModel: each model's inputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, outputTokens, costUSD from modelUsage, as reported
method.toolCalls: the distinct toolUseId values on "tool_dispatch_start" lines in the --debug-file log; null when the session took more than one turn and the log has no such line, and such runs are left out of the tool-call figures
method.inBrief: per question, whether its rule id appears in the text of the default `chamoji memory brief` in the clone with chamoji set up, the brief its sessions receive

questions.question: May I add a new top-level folder to the tree in `refs/chamoji/memory`?
questions.label: A new folder in the memory ref
questions.key: No: the layout is fixed until a new format gets its own ref or a version bump, because older clients drop what they don't know.

questions.question: Should `chamoji init` set `remote.origin.push` so a plain `git push` also pushes memory?
questions.label: Init setting the push refspec
questions.key: No: it must not set it, and the fetch refspec must be a wildcard, or plain push, fetch and pull break.

questions.question: Why does the command in the Claude Code hook entries end in `|| true`?
questions.label: Why the hooks end in `|| true`
questions.key: Claude Code reads exit 2 as a block; a denial is JSON on stdout with exit 0 and still gets through.

questions.question: Can I add the official MCP SDK as a dependency for `chamoji mcp`?
questions.label: Adding the MCP SDK
questions.key: No: it would double chamoji's install for five methods.

questions.question: Why does `chamoji why` blame the working copy and not HEAD?
questions.label: Why `chamoji why` blames the work tree
questions.key: So line numbers match the editor, and an edited line is reported as uncommitted.

Claude Code treats a hook's exit code 2 as a block, so if the chamoji command failed with that code it could stop the agent's work. Ending both command forms in `|| true` forces exit 0. A real denial is still delivered as JSON on stdout with exit 0, so it gets through.

I relied on constraint c-f3ea2f10 (commit 800050c), and on c-5833401c (commit 6617b21), which says the hook must always exit 0 so a broken hook never stops the agent.

The `|| true` forces the hook to exit 0. A chamoji older than the `agent-hook` command prints help and exits 2, which Claude Code treats as "block this". The hook file is committed, so that would block every commit. A real denial still gets through, because it is JSON on stdout with exit 0. I got this from the comment above `runChamoji` at `packages/cli/src/init.ts:170-178`. I didn't check the commits or ledger rules (which the benchmark data cites as c-f3ea2f10 / commit 800050c).

The `|| true` is there because an older installed chamoji doesn't know the `agent-hook` command, so it prints help and exits 2. Claude Code reads exit 2 as "block this", and since `.claude/settings.json` is committed, that would block every commit. A real denial is still delivered as JSON on stdout with exit 0, so it gets through.

It blames the working copy so that line numbers match what you see in the editor. It also means an edited but uncommitted line is reported as uncommitted, instead of being blamed on an older commit. This comes from constraint `c-7a4d905c` on commit `2fd0da6` ("✨ Add chamoji why to explain a line").

`chamoji why` runs `git blame` with no revision (`packages/core/src/blame.ts:49-54`), so git blames the working copy. That way the `<file>:<line>` number matches what an editor shows, even when the file has uncommitted edits. A line that isn't committed yet then reports as `uncommitted` instead of being blamed on the wrong commit. The readme's `why` section (`readme.md:191`) describes the same behavior. I didn't find a specific commit or rule that records why it was chosen, only the code comment and the readme.

`chamoji why` blames the working copy so that the line numbers match what an editor shows, including after uncommitted edits. Blaming a revision such as HEAD would count lines in the committed file, which can differ from the open one. The relevant code is `blameLine` in `packages/core/src/blame.ts:49`, where a comment says it passes no revision for this reason. The readme (line 191) says the same, and a line you haven't committed yet is reported as uncommitted instead of being blamed on some commit. I didn't find a specific commit that introduced this choice.
